reading.body:
James Justice's AI record is two cosponsorships and twelve recorded votes, with no sponsored AI bill of his own.

The two cosponsorships are the only affirmative legislative acts in the set: S. 5117, the Senior Chatbot Protection Act of 2026, and S. 3586, the AI for Mainstreet Act. Everything else is a vote on a single bill, S. 2296, whose short title is not on file. The votes cluster on three dates in September and October 2025, and they split. He voted Yea on cloture, on the motion to proceed, on the motion to table an amendment, and on final passage. He voted Nay on six amendments and Yea on two others. Final passage is the one that matters most, because it is the only vote in the set that would have sent the bill forward as a whole.

For AI specifically, the record shows a legislator engaging with AI-adjacent bills at the amendment level rather than the authorship level. The two cosponsorships name AI directly, one on chatbots and one on small business adoption. The vote series does not, because S. 2296 carries no short title in the data, so nothing here establishes that the bill concerns AI at all. The record also contains no money, despite the summary describing AI company and AI-focused political committee contributions as part of what the site holds. No contribution, amount, or donor appears in the events.

What this does not tell a reader is why any vote went the way it did, what the amendments would have done, or whether the two cosponsored bills advanced. It covers one senator's dated actions and nothing about compute, data centers, or power.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for James Justice: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 14 events.
